Description: COM and SCPU application firmware content and version, including update packages installed via IoT Core
Threat description: An attacker impersonates a trusted firmware source to deliver a malicious firmware image via the IoT Core update mechanism.
Rationale: SRIO-7915 documents firmware installation over IoT Core; no independent update-source authentication process is documented in the provided files.
Test Objective: Submit a firmware image from an unauthorized/spoofed source and verify rejection, alerting, and no installation.

Description: COM and SCPU bootloader code responsible for controlled startup and firmware acceptance
Threat description: An attacker uses the documented per-controller debug/programming interface to impersonate a legitimate flashing tool and load unauthorized bootloader code.
Rationale: SRIO-1374 documents a debug and firmware-flashing interface for each controller; no bootloader source-authentication mechanism is documented for this interface.
Test Objective: Attempt bootloader replacement via the debug/flashing interface from an unauthorized tool and verify rejection or detection.

Description: Configured own PROFIsafe safety address (F_Dest_Add) set via rotary switches, used for safety communication identity binding
Threat description: A rogue device is configured with a duplicated or forged F-Address to be accepted as a valid safety communication partner.
Rationale: F_Dest_Add is the own safety address configurable via rotary switches (SRIO-2013) and used for F-Parameter identity binding.
Test Objective: Introduce a device with a duplicated F-Address and verify detection/rejection before safety communication is established.

Description: CRC-protected safety parameter set (F_WD_Time, F_Source_Add, F_iParCRC, F_ParCRC, and safety iParameters such as Filter Time, Symmetry, Discrepancy Time, Switch-off Delay)
Threat description: An attacker impersonates an authorized F-Engineering tool to submit a fraudulent safety parameter set.
Rationale: The F-Parameter record (table 6) and iParameter CRC (F_iParCRC) are documented as transferred from an F-Engineering Tool with no independent tool-authentication step described.
Test Objective: Submit a safety parameter set from an unauthorized engineering source and verify rejection and CRC/authenticity validation.

Description: Safety digital input process values exchanged via PROFIsafe/PROFINET
Threat description: An attacker injects fabricated safety digital input values impersonating a legitimate field sensor/source.
Rationale: F-DI channels and their PROFIsafe transport are explicitly documented (100 Sec. 8.3, 209 Sec. 6.2.3).
Test Objective: Inject spoofed F-DI values and verify PROFIsafe address/CRC validation rejects them before use.

Description: Safety digital output command values exchanged via PROFIsafe/PROFINET
Threat description: An attacker impersonates the F-Host/PLC to send forged safety output commands.
Rationale: F-DO channels and F_Source_Add-based host identity are explicitly documented (100 Sec. 8.4, 209 F-Parameter table).
Test Objective: Send forged F-DO commands from an unauthorized source and verify rejection before actuation.

Description: PROFINET communication identity and network configuration (NameOfStation, IP suite, default gateway)
Threat description: An attacker impersonates a PROFINET IO-Controller or Engineering System to issue DCP set operations.
Rationale: DCP set of IP parameters/NameOfStation by an IO-Controller or Engineering System is explicitly documented (SRIO-3029).
Test Objective: Issue DCP set requests from an unauthorized host and verify rejection, alerting, and no unauthorized parameter change.

Description: Device identity attributes (serial number, product code/name, vendor, hardware/software revisions, production date)
Threat description: An attacker presents forged device identity data to masquerade as a genuine SRIO unit.
Rationale: Deviceinfo tree fields are explicitly documented as identity data relied upon by engineering/asset-management systems (SRIO-2946).
Test Objective: Present forged identity data to management interfaces and verify identity-consistency checks or detection.

Description: PROFINET Identification & Maintenance records (I&M0-I&M4), including I&M4 safety CRC linkage
Threat description: An attacker provides forged I&M data to misrepresent device identity/maintenance information to PROFINET engineering tools.
Rationale: I&M0-I&M4 are explicitly documented standard PROFINET identification/maintenance records (209 Sec. 6.3.1.1, SRIO-3015).
Test Objective: Present manipulated I&M records and verify consistency/validation checks against actual device data.

Description: Device description file (GSDML) used for PROFINET engineering integration, including F_ParamDescCRC
Threat description: An attacker distributes a modified GSDML file impersonating the authentic ifm-provided engineering descriptor.
Rationale: GSDML filename/version content and the F_ParamDescCRC attribute are explicitly specified (SRIO-3019, SRIO-7758).
Test Objective: Substitute a modified GSDML file in the engineering workflow and verify detection via checksum/version verification.

Description: COM and SCPU application firmware content and version, including update packages installed via IoT Core
Threat description: An attacker modifies firmware content in transit or at rest before or after installation.
Rationale: SRIO-7915 documents firmware installation and version tracking (swrevision) without a described in-transit/at-rest integrity check.
Test Objective: Inject modified firmware content and verify integrity validation prevents installation or execution.

Description: COM and SCPU bootloader code responsible for controlled startup and firmware acceptance
Threat description: An attacker modifies bootloader code via the documented per-controller debug/flashing interface.
Rationale: SRIO-1374 documents a debug and firmware-flashing interface for each controller; no bootloader integrity-verification mechanism is documented.
Test Objective: Attempt bootloader modification via the debug/flashing interface and verify rejection or detection.

Description: Configured own PROFIsafe safety address (F_Dest_Add) set via rotary switches, used for safety communication identity binding
Threat description: A person changes rotary switch values or the engineering-side F-Address configuration to alter the safety address without authorization.
Rationale: The rotary switch function and its mapping to the own safe address (F_Dest_Add) are explicitly specified (SRIO-2013, 209 F-Parameter table).
Test Objective: Change the configured F-Address without authorization and verify detection, controlled acceptance rules, and diagnostics.

Description: CRC-protected safety parameter set (F_WD_Time, F_Source_Add, F_iParCRC, F_ParCRC, and safety iParameters such as Filter Time, Symmetry, Discrepancy Time, Switch-off Delay)
Threat description: An attacker modifies F_WD_Time, F_Source_Add, F_iParCRC/F_ParCRC, or associated safety iParameters.
Rationale: The F-Parameter record and iParameter tables (209 table 6; 100 Sec. 8.3/8.4; SRIO-19971) define these as changeable, CRC-protected values.
Test Objective: Inject modified parameter/iParameter values and verify CRC/consistency validation and rejection before activation.

Description: Safety digital input process values exchanged via PROFIsafe/PROFINET
Threat description: An attacker modifies safety input values in transit before they reach the controller.
Rationale: F-DI channels and their PROFIsafe transport are explicitly documented (100 Sec. 8.3, 209 Sec. 6.2.3).
Test Objective: Inject modified F-DI values and verify detection/rejection before unsafe processing.

Description: Safety digital output command values exchanged via PROFIsafe/PROFINET
Threat description: An attacker modifies safety output commands before they reach the device.
Rationale: F-DO channels and output parameterization are explicitly documented (100 Sec. 8.4, 209 Sec. 6.2.4).
Test Objective: Inject modified F-DO commands and verify detection/rejection before unsafe actuation.

Description: RIOforFA channel qualifier bits bound to F-DI/F-DO process values
Threat description: An attacker desynchronizes the RIOforFA Qualifier from its associated Value, breaking the required Value/Qualifier consistency.
Rationale: SRIO-3028 explicitly requires that "the Qualifier shall be synchronous and consistent with the Value" for RIOforFA channels.
Test Objective: Manipulate qualifier bits independent of the associated value and verify consistency enforcement or detection.

Description: PROFINET communication identity and network configuration (NameOfStation, IP suite, default gateway)
Threat description: An attacker modifies NameOfStation or IP parameters using unauthorized DCP parameter writes.
Rationale: DCP parameter setting is documented and directly affects communication identity and reachability (SRIO-3029).
Test Objective: Issue unauthorized DCP writes and verify integrity protection, change authorization, and diagnosable rejection.

Description: User-assigned application tag (devicetag/applicationtag) used for asset identification
Threat description: An attacker modifies the application tag without authorization, misleading asset tracking or maintenance processes.
Rationale: The devicetag/applicationtag element is documented as a read-write IoT element (SRIO-2955).
Test Objective: Attempt unauthorized devicetag modification and verify access-control enforcement.

Description: Device error log content (ErrorEvents and Uptime) accessible via IoT Core
Threat description: An attacker alters or clears logged error events to hide malicious activity or a fault condition.
Rationale: Error log content and SysCom timeout events are documented as logged and IoT-readable (SRIO-10662, SRIO-15221, 209 line ~358).
Test Objective: Attempt unauthorized log modification/deletion and verify tamper evidence and retention behavior.

Description: Operational status and diagnostic telemetry (operating state, temperature, voltage, current, rotary switch reading)
Threat description: An attacker falsifies reported operating state or diagnostic telemetry to mask a fault or unsafe condition.
Rationale: The devicestatus tree explicitly defines operatingstate, temperature, voltage, and current fields (SRIO-2950).
Test Objective: Attempt to manipulate reported status values and verify integrity protection or detection.

Description: PROFINET Identification & Maintenance records (I&M0-I&M4), including I&M4 safety CRC linkage
Threat description: An attacker modifies I&M4 data, which carries the F_iParCRC and F_ParCRC values, undermining safety-parameter integrity verification.
Rationale: The COM specification explicitly states I&M4 Data is a string containing F_iParCRC and F_ParCRC values (209, I&M4 description).
Test Objective: Modify I&M4 content and verify cross-validation against the actual F-Parameter CRC values.

Description: Configuration, identity, and state data persisted in EEPROM and restored at startup
Threat description: An attacker modifies remanent data stored in EEPROM without authorization, altering restored configuration, identity, or state.
Rationale: The IO-Delegator retrieves remanent (persistent) data stored in EEPROM during startup (209 Sec. 2.3.4.3-2.3.4.4).
Test Objective: Attempt unauthorized persistent-data modification and verify detection, rejection, and safe startup behavior.

Description: Device description file (GSDML) used for PROFINET engineering integration, including F_ParamDescCRC
Threat description: An attacker modifies GSDML content (module IDs, F_ParamDescCRC) causing incorrect engineering-time safety parameter validation.
Rationale: Module/submodule IDs and the F_ParamDescCRC attribute are explicitly specified (SRIO-2973, SRIO-2975, SRIO-7758).
Test Objective: Modify GSDML fields and verify the engineering tool detects a mismatch against device-reported values.

Description: COM and SCPU application firmware content and version, including update packages installed via IoT Core
Threat description: A user denies having triggered or approved a firmware installation.
Rationale: Firmware installation over IoT Core and the FW_UPDATE state are documented (SRIO-7915, 100 line 1552-1553) without a described per-action attribution record.
Test Objective: Perform a firmware update and verify an attributable, timestamped audit trail for the initiating action.

Description: Configured own PROFIsafe safety address (F_Dest_Add) set via rotary switches, used for safety communication identity binding
Threat description: A technician denies having changed the configured safety address.
Rationale: F-Address configuration via rotary switches is a documented safety-relevant action (SRIO-2013) with no described attribution logging.
Test Objective: Change the configured F-Address and verify an attributable record of who performed the change and when.

Description: CRC-protected safety parameter set (F_WD_Time, F_Source_Add, F_iParCRC, F_ParCRC, and safety iParameters such as Filter Time, Symmetry, Discrepancy Time, Switch-off Delay)
Threat description: An engineering user denies having modified safety parameters.
Rationale: The F-Parameter/iParameter set is documented as user-changeable via an engineering tool (209 table 6) without described per-change attribution.
Test Objective: Change a safety parameter and verify an attributable, timestamped audit trail for the change.

Description: PROFINET communication identity and network configuration (NameOfStation, IP suite, default gateway)
Threat description: A user denies having changed the IP address or NameOfStation configuration.
Rationale: DCP-based parameter changes by an IO-Controller/Engineering System are documented (SRIO-3029) without described per-action attribution.
Test Objective: Change network configuration and verify an attributable record of the responsible actor.

Description: Device error log content (ErrorEvents and Uptime) accessible via IoT Core
Threat description: A user denies having cleared or altered logged error events.
Rationale: Error log content is documented as service-accessible via IoT (SRIO-10662, SRIO-15221) without a described tamper-evidence/attribution guarantee for log-management actions.
Test Objective: Clear or alter log entries and verify an attributable, tamper-evident record of the management action itself.

Description: COM and SCPU application firmware content and version, including update packages installed via IoT Core
Threat description: An unauthorized party reads the exact firmware version to identify exploitable, version-specific vulnerabilities.
Rationale: The swrevision field is explicitly documented as an IoT-readable deviceinfo element (SRIO-2946).
Test Objective: Attempt unauthorized readout of firmware version data and verify access control and data minimization.

Description: COM and SCPU bootloader code responsible for controlled startup and firmware acceptance
Threat description: An unauthorized party reads bootloader version information to target known bootloader weaknesses.
Rationale: The cpubootloaderversion and scpubootloaderversion fields are explicitly documented IoT-readable elements (209 deviceinfo/swinfo table).
Test Objective: Attempt unauthorized readout of bootloader version data and verify access control.

Description: Configured own PROFIsafe safety address (F_Dest_Add) set via rotary switches, used for safety communication identity binding
Threat description: An unauthorized party reads the configured rotary-switch/F-Address value to plan a duplicate-address attack.
Rationale: The rotary_switch value is explicitly documented as an IoT-readable devicestatus element (SRIO-2950).
Test Objective: Attempt unauthorized readout of the rotary switch/F-Address value and verify access restriction.

Description: CRC-protected safety parameter set (F_WD_Time, F_Source_Add, F_iParCRC, F_ParCRC, and safety iParameters such as Filter Time, Symmetry, Discrepancy Time, Switch-off Delay)
Threat description: An attacker obtains safety parameter values and valid CRC ranges via the engineering channel/GSDML to craft a plausible malicious parameter set.
Rationale: F-Parameter and iParameter value ranges and CRC fields are explicitly specified in the GSD/engineering documentation (209 table 6).
Test Objective: Attempt unauthorized access to safety parameter values and verify access restriction and data minimization.

Description: Safety digital input process values (and associated Qualifier bits) exchanged via PROFIsafe/PROFINET
Threat description: An attacker passively captures fieldbus traffic to learn live input states and associated qualifier information.
Rationale: F-DI channels and RIOforFA Value/Qualifier mapping are explicitly documented (100 Sec. 8.3, SRIO-3028).
Test Objective: Sniff fieldbus traffic from an unauthorized vantage point and verify confidentiality controls or compensating protections.

Description: Safety digital output command values (and associated Qualifier bits) exchanged via PROFIsafe/PROFINET
Threat description: An attacker passively captures fieldbus traffic to learn output actuation states and associated qualifier information.
Rationale: F-DO channels and RIOforFA Value/Qualifier mapping are explicitly documented (100 Sec. 8.4, SRIO-3028).
Test Objective: Sniff fieldbus traffic from an unauthorized vantage point and verify confidentiality controls or compensating protections.

Description: PROFINET communication identity and network configuration (NameOfStation, IP suite, default gateway)
Threat description: An attacker reads network configuration data for reconnaissance of the automation network topology.
Rationale: The fieldbussetup/network tree (including ipdefaultgateway) and DCP identity data are explicitly documented (209 line ~835).
Test Objective: Attempt unauthorized readout of network configuration values and verify access restriction.

Description: User-assigned application tag (devicetag/applicationtag) used for asset identification
Threat description: An attacker reads the application tag to learn deployment context (e.g., factory/machine naming).
Rationale: The devicetag/applicationtag element and its example value are explicitly documented (SRIO-2955).
Test Objective: Attempt unauthorized readout of the devicetag value and verify access restriction.

Description: Device error log content (ErrorEvents and Uptime) accessible via IoT Core
Threat description: Unauthorized access to error-log details reveals internal failure modes and attack-relevant information.
Rationale: Error log content is documented as readable via IoT and understandable to users (SRIO-10662, SRIO-15221).
Test Objective: Attempt unauthorized error-log access and verify access restriction and data minimization.

Description: Operational status and diagnostic telemetry (operating state, temperature, voltage, current, rotary switch reading)
Threat description: An unauthorized party reads operating state and environmental telemetry to profile device conditions and plan attacks.
Rationale: The devicestatus tree explicitly defines these fields as IoT-readable (SRIO-2950).
Test Objective: Attempt unauthorized readout of devicestatus values and verify access restriction.

Description: Device identity attributes (serial number, product code/name, vendor, hardware/software revisions, production date)
Threat description: An attacker reads device identity data to target specific product/version combinations.
Rationale: The deviceinfo tree explicitly defines these fields as IoT-readable (SRIO-2946).
Test Objective: Attempt unauthorized readout of deviceinfo values and verify access restriction.

Description: PROFINET Identification & Maintenance records (I&M0-I&M4), including I&M4 safety CRC linkage
Threat description: An attacker reads I&M records, including I&M4 safety CRC linkage data, to support crafting of a tampered safety parameter set.
Rationale: I&M0-I&M4 records and the I&M4 F_iParCRC/F_ParCRC content are explicitly documented (209 Sec. 6.3.1.1, I&M4 description).
Test Objective: Attempt unauthorized access to I&M records and verify access restriction, particularly for I&M4 CRC content.

Description: Configuration, identity, and state data persisted in EEPROM and restored at startup
Threat description: An attacker with physical or debug-level access extracts persisted configuration/identity/state data directly from EEPROM.
Rationale: EEPROM is documented as the persistent-data storage restored at startup (209 Sec. 2.3.4.3-2.3.4.4, hardware table).
Test Objective: Attempt unauthorized extraction of EEPROM content and verify protection against direct storage-level disclosure.

Description: COM and SCPU application firmware content and version, including update packages installed via IoT Core
Threat description: An attacker disrupts or corrupts the firmware update process, leaving the device unable to complete installation.
Rationale: A dedicated FW_UPDATE state handles the firmware update process (100 line 1552-1553); disruption during this state is a documented control point.
Test Objective: Disrupt the update process at various stages and verify safe recovery, rollback, or bounded retry behavior.

Description: COM and SCPU bootloader code responsible for controlled startup and firmware acceptance
Threat description: An attacker corrupts or interrupts bootloader operation via the debug/flashing interface, preventing device startup.
Rationale: SRIO-1374 documents a debug/firmware-flashing interface per controller that provides a direct path to bootloader disruption.
Test Objective: Attempt bootloader disruption via the debug/flashing interface and verify safe-state handling and recovery.

Description: CRC-protected safety parameter set (F_WD_Time, F_Source_Add, F_iParCRC, F_ParCRC, and safety iParameters such as Filter Time, Symmetry, Discrepancy Time, Switch-off Delay)
Threat description: An attacker repeatedly submits invalid safety parameter sets, causing recurring channel/device passivation and preventing stable operation.
Rationale: F_Passivation (Channel and Device granular) is the explicitly documented safety response to parameter/validation conditions (209 F-Parameter table, SRIO-14858, SRIO-14857).
Test Objective: Repeatedly submit invalid safety parameter sets and verify throttling/lockout controls and resilient recovery behavior.

Description: Safety digital input process values exchanged via PROFIsafe/PROFINET
Threat description: An attacker floods or blocks communication, preventing timely delivery of safety input data.
Rationale: Overcurrent-triggered port shutdown and diagnosis behavior for inputs are explicitly documented (100 line 822).
Test Objective: Apply excessive/malformed traffic or fault conditions and verify graceful degradation, diagnostics, and safe-state handling.

Description: Safety digital output command values exchanged via PROFIsafe/PROFINET
Threat description: An attacker repeatedly triggers documented single-output-failure/overcurrent shutdown behavior to keep outputs unavailable.
Rationale: Single output failure switch-off and re-acknowledgement requirements are explicitly documented (100 lines 959-985).
Test Objective: Repeatedly trigger output fault conditions and verify bounded impact, controlled recovery, and no cascading failure.

Description: PROFINET communication identity and network configuration (NameOfStation, IP suite, default gateway)
Threat description: An attacker issues unauthorized DCP reset commands that repeatedly clear communication parameters, causing loss of connectivity.
Rationale: DCP reset modes (Mode 1-9) explicitly reset communication parameters, engineering data, and in some modes installed software (209 lines 942-968).
Test Objective: Issue unauthorized DCP reset commands and verify strict authorization, controlled execution, and recovery behavior.

Description: Device error log content (ErrorEvents and Uptime) accessible via IoT Core
Threat description: An attacker generates excessive fault/error events to fill the finite system log buffer, potentially evicting forensically relevant entries.
Rationale: A "system log buffer" for logged events is explicitly referenced (209 line ~358).
Test Objective: Generate a high rate of loggable events and verify bounded buffer handling and preservation of relevant entries.

Description: Operational status and diagnostic telemetry (operating state, temperature, voltage, current, rotary switch reading)
Threat description: An attacker exhausts the limited number of concurrent HTTP connections, blocking legitimate access to status/diagnostic data.
Rationale: The device supports only incoming connections and limits active HTTP connections to two (SRIO-7908, SRIO-7909).
Test Objective: Open parallel sessions beyond the documented limit and verify controlled refusal and recovery of legitimate access.

Description: Configuration, identity, and state data persisted in EEPROM and restored at startup
Threat description: An attacker corrupts persisted data so that configuration/identity/state cannot be correctly restored after a power cycle or restart.
Rationale: The NVMEM Delegator explicitly supports "restoration of saved system states after power cycles or restarts" (209 Sec. 2.3.4.4).
Test Objective: Corrupt persisted data and verify detection, safe defaults, and controlled recovery behavior at next startup.

Description: COM and SCPU application firmware content and version, including update packages installed via IoT Core
Threat description: A user without firmware-update rights triggers installation of a firmware image.
Rationale: The IoT tree rights model explicitly distinguishes Read, Write, and Service rights for elements including /firmware (209 rights glossary, SRIO-2938).
Test Objective: Attempt firmware installation from a read-only/unprivileged context and verify strict authorization enforcement.

Description: COM and SCPU bootloader code responsible for controlled startup and firmware acceptance
Threat description: An attacker uses the debug/flashing interface to obtain control beyond normal operational access rights.
Rationale: SRIO-1374 documents a debug/firmware-flashing interface per controller as a distinct, more privileged access path than normal operation.
Test Objective: Attempt privileged flashing operations from an unprivileged operational context and verify strict access control enforcement.

Description: Configured own PROFIsafe safety address (F_Dest_Add) set via rotary switches, used for safety communication identity binding
Threat description: An actor with only diagnostic/read access (e.g., rotary_switch status readout) escalates to modify the configured F-Address.
Rationale: The IoT/DCP model distinguishes read-only status elements from write-capable configuration paths (209 rights glossary; SRIO-2013).
Test Objective: Attempt F-Address modification from a read-only diagnostic context and verify strict authorization enforcement.

Description: CRC-protected safety parameter set (F_WD_Time, F_Source_Add, F_iParCRC, F_ParCRC, and safety iParameters such as Filter Time, Symmetry, Discrepancy Time, Switch-off Delay)
Threat description: An actor with diagnostic-only access escalates to safety-parameter write access via the engineering channel.
Rationale: Safety parameters are documented as changeable via engineering tools (209 table 6) distinct from read-only diagnostic elements in the rights model.
Test Objective: Attempt safety-parameter modification from a diagnostic-only context and verify strict authorization enforcement.

Description: PROFINET communication identity and network configuration (NameOfStation, IP suite, default gateway)
Threat description: An actor with read-only network visibility escalates to DCP write access over network configuration.
Rationale: DCP setting of IP/NameOfStation is documented as a controller/engineering function (SRIO-3029) distinct from read-only status/deviceinfo elements.
Test Objective: Attempt network configuration changes from a read-only context and verify strict authorization enforcement.

Description: RIOforFA channel qualifier bits bound to F-DI/F-DO process values
Threat description: An attacker forges qualifier bits while presenting them as legitimate channel-validity information.
Rationale: SRIO-3028 requires qualifier information to be synchronous and consistent with values, making authenticity of qualifier bits security-relevant.
Test Objective: Inject forged qualifier bits and verify acceptance is denied when source/authenticity checks fail.

Description: COM and SCPU bootloader code responsible for controlled startup and firmware acceptance
Threat description: A technician denies having performed bootloader flashing via the documented debug/programming interface.
Rationale: SRIO-1374 documents a debug and firmware-flashing interface per controller; attributable records for flashing actions are not documented in provided artifacts.
Test Objective: Execute a bootloader flashing action and verify attributable, timestamped, tamper-evident audit evidence for the actor.

Description: User-assigned application tag (devicetag/applicationtag) used for asset identification
Threat description: A user denies having changed the device application tag.
Rationale: The device tag is documented as read-write (SRIO-2955), but no explicit per-change attribution mechanism is documented.
Test Objective: Change the device tag and verify attributable logging of actor, time, previous value, and new value.

Description: RIOforFA channel qualifier bits bound to F-DI/F-DO process values
Threat description: An attacker observes qualifier-bit patterns to infer channel health, fault handling behavior, and process-state confidence.
Rationale: SRIO-3028 defines qualifier semantics as part of process channels, so unauthorized disclosure can reveal operational and diagnostic context.
Test Objective: Capture qualifier traffic from an unauthorized vantage point and verify confidentiality controls or compensating restrictions.

Description: Configured own PROFIsafe safety address (F_Dest_Add) set via rotary switches, used for safety communication identity binding
Threat description: An attacker sets an incorrect/duplicated F-Address so safety communication fails or repeatedly passivates.
Rationale: F_Dest_Add identity binding and rotary-switch based own-safe-address configuration are documented; mismatches disrupt safety communication establishment.
Test Objective: Apply incorrect or duplicate F-Address settings and verify diagnostics, rejection, and controlled recovery.

Description: RIOforFA channel qualifier bits bound to F-DI/F-DO process values
Threat description: An attacker manipulates or blocks qualifier bits to force repeated invalid-channel interpretation and loss of usable process data.
Rationale: SRIO-3028 requires valid Value/Qualifier consistency for RIOforFA channels; repeated qualifier invalidation can deny normal operation.
Test Objective: Disrupt qualifier delivery/consistency and verify bounded fail-safe behavior and robust recovery.
